object_description: two rotated eight-level volumes enclosing a dense central heart
design_condition: The built masses are concentrated west of the site, leaving the eastern perimeter open for walks, sports, and landscape, while establishing an axial dialogue with neighbouring monumental buildings.

positive.statement: The urban and morphological concept establishes an equivalent relationship with the existing prison and a striking dialogue with the neighbouring building.
The concentration of the built masses frees a significant surface area of the site.
The formal system connects the essential elements with great consistency and supports the proper functioning of the establishment.
The cellular spaces are carefully considered, freed from parasitic accessories, and opened unhindered toward the sky and landscape.

negative.statement: The landscaped treatment of the open site is insufficiently developed, and the necessary privacy between walks is difficult to achieve.
The density of activity and concentration of people generated by the system are not considered credible.
The provision of natural light to the lower floors is not convincing.
The guards and prisoners would be confined within a perfectly controlled but oppressive architectural system.
The high number of floors would create significant difficulties for prisoner movement and transfers.
The complexity of the cellular facades makes the construction cost significantly higher than the target.
The built density makes phased construction of the cellular building problematic.
